title: Gpt5 made me a doom style game
author: heavyfyzx
selftext: Nothing too advanced, but it came up with this doom style game. I will be exploring this more. I've already made a dungeon crawler with procedurally generating loot, multiple player classes, skills trees, and a shop with item sets that give a bonus. Gpt5 is crazy. I dont use it for conversations.

replies.author: evilbarron2
replies.body:
And yet 95% of companies using ChatGPT are seeing no benefit. I’m sure they’re all just using it wrong, right?

I think people are starting to realize that AI is a feature, not a product

replies.author: sibarino
replies.body:
95% of companies using GENERATIVE AI  in workflows are doomed to fail.

If you really think that AI is not being effectively used in industry settings idk what to tell you.
Most AI use is on things like replacing large computations with internal models, identifying faulty equipment from images, these kinds of uses.

The media driven debate of GENERATIVE AI and AI has a whole in industry are two insanely disconnected things.
I would never expect a media or entertainment based company to succeed using AI because half their product should be effort.

replies.author: evilbarron2
replies.body:
This seems a strange argument: you’re effectively saying your (presumably limited) personal experience trumps the findings of a broad survey carried out by the MIT Media Lab division devoted to AI. 

I don’t find this a compelling argument.

I agree that AI as it currently stands is a powerful and even transformative tool. I also believe that - like any new technology at this stage - we don’t really know how to use it yet. The claims of AI creating a massive discontinuity or “singularity” are silly, akin to the Y2K drama. But to pin that on “the media” is serious retconning - this hype was manufactured solely and repeatedly by leaders in the AI industry itself.

replies.author: sibarino
replies.body:
While the headlines may vary. The actual conclusion of the survey you are referring to is that 95% of GENERATIVE AI pilots are failing. If you look at the listed companies they are media-oriented.

I am not disagreeing with this result, I simply clarified these two points. 

The most lucrative uses of AI at the moment are not generative or media related.

replies.author: evilbarron2
replies.body: I believe this argument is called “special pleading”. I don’t have access to the report right now, but when I read it I’m pretty sure the used “Generative AI” to include LLMs, not making a distinction between image creation AI and LLMs. Makes sense: if you wanted to evaluate only image- and video-generating AI, you wouldn’t ask Fortune 500 companies. You’d focus on movie studios, production companies, and advertising agencies. I’m pretty confident the bright folks at MIT Media Lab wouldn’t make that mistake.
